attempts.summary: On node1, /srv/data is now backed by a dedicated loop-backed LVM logical volume (datavg/datalv on /dev/loop0, XFS). Baseline app data was written, an LVM snapshot (datalv_snap) captured that state, /srv/data was then modified (a file deleted, a file overwritten, a file corrupted, an unexpected file added), and the LVM snapshot was merged back into the origin to restore the exact pre-modification content — verified via matching sha256 checksums. Persistence across reboot was arranged (systemd unit srvdata-loop-attach.service reattaches the loop device and activates the VG before local-fs mounting; /etc/fstab mounts /dev/mapper/datavg-datalv at /srv/data). The mandatory restart protocol was completed for node1: boot_id changed from f455a75c-ec12-49a8-a647-c2be3f67c08c to 660dca51-3ccd-4408-a026-7b978e389d05, and post-reboot verification shows /srv/data auto-recovered with content identical to the snapshot baseline.
